close_reason:
Substantially addressed by bd:JMAP-26di.5's commit c626efa, which delegated both chat_capability and chat_push_capability to the foundation helper account.account_extension_capability::<T>(URI). Each function is now 4 lines (account lookup early-return + one-line delegate), and the duplicated body (the bead's original target) is eliminated.

The remaining 3-line account-lookup boilerplate exists because the foundation helper is on AccountInfo, not Session. Pushing the entire helper to Session-level (so callers can write 'session.account_extension_capability::<T>(account_id, URI)') is a foundation-crate change with workspace-wide propagation implications — not in scope for this chat-client review epic.

The workspace-template-propagation aspect remains a valid follow-up: sibling extension-client crates (jmap-mail-client, jmap-calendars-client, etc.) likely have the same 4-line shape post-.5-style refactor and could benefit from a Session-level helper landing in jmap-base-client. Filing as out-of-scope for this review pass; closing this bead.
description: session.rs:179-213 — chat_capability and chat_push_capability differ only in the capability URI string and the typed return value. Same null-check chain, same Option<T> handling, same map_err. A generic helper 'fn parse_account_capability<C: for<'de> Deserialize<'de>>(session: &Session, account_id: &str, capability_uri: &str) -> Result<Option<C>, ClientError>' would consolidate the two into 4-line wrappers. Engineering basis: DRY — two copies will drift; adding any third capability (e.g. ChatWebsocketCapability if its shape becomes structured rather than empty) will copy-paste the body again. The base-client (jmap-base-client) is a natural place for the helper since it owns the Session type. Workspace-template-propagation candidate — sibling extension-client crates (jmap-mail-client, jmap-calendars-client, etc.) likely have the same shape.
title: session.rs chat_capability and chat_push_capability bodies are near-identical
